name: Diablo
license: SDK/ROS2: Apache-2.0; STL/SDF and RL URDF repos: no licence file (all rights reserved)
leg_topology: Per leg: hip and knee-drive motors coaxial at the body, with a four-bar (parallelogram-style) linkage carrying the knee drive. 3 DOF per leg (hip, knee, wheel). No hip abduction. Crouched height 270 mm.
leg_motors: 4x DDT M1502D direct drive (24 V, 9.6 Nm rated, >=17 Nm stall, 115 rpm rated, >=200 rpm no-load)
battery: Li-ion 32 V 6 Ah (~192 Wh derived); ~3 h standing, ~4 h creeping travel, ~15 min squatting
notes: Wheel diameter is 200 mm from the simplified RL URDF (wheel radius 0.1 m, thigh/shank 0.14 m each, efforts 27 Nm, 26 rad/s). The SDF has the real linkage. Speed 2 m/s, jump 8 cm. M1502D sells separately for $310 (backorder). Compute is a Raspberry Pi in the MYBOTSHOP integration. ROS 2 is recommended.

name: TITA
license: tita_rl: MIT; TITA_Description URDF and DDT_Lab: no licence file
leg_topology: Serial leg with hip abduction (+/-45 deg), hip pitch, knee and wheel: 4 DOF per leg, 8 total. Reconfigurable to quadruped modes.
leg_motors: Quasi-direct-drive joint modules, 120 Nm peak (model unknown)
wheel_motors: QDD module (part of the 8 DOF; model unknown)
battery: 43.2 V nominal; 1 h per pack; 2 hot-swappable packs
notes: Mass 24.1 kg is without battery; the URDF sums to ~27.7 kg (derived). Wheel radius 0.0925 m from the URDF. Speed 3 m/s, jump 30 cm (another listing says 20 cm). Jetson Orin NX 16GB, ROS 2 + Zenoh. Richest public RL tooling (Isaac Gym MIT; Isaac Lab DDT_Lab unlicensed).

name: Ascento (ICRA 2019 research robot)
leg_topology: One hip motor per leg driving an optimised three-bar linkage that approximates vertical wheel travel. Torsion springs for gravity compensation and jumping. No knee motor, no abduction.
leg_motors: 2x ANYbotics ANYdrive series-elastic actuators, 40 Nm peak
wheel_motors: 2x Maxon EC90 frameless direct-drive hub motors, 3.5 Nm max, EPOS4 controllers
battery: 4x 3S LiPo 5000 mAh in series (motors) + 4S 2200 mAh LiPo (compute); ~1.5 h
notes: Height adjustable 310-660 mm. SLS PA12 topology-optimised parts. Intel NUC i7, LQR control. Jump ~0.4 m (New Atlas). RL stair-climbing follow-up in Isaac Gym needed 20 ms delay simulation. Commercial Ascento Pro/Guard specs differ.

name: Upkie
leg_topology: Serial 2-link leg: hip motor at torso, knee motor carried on the femur, wheel motor at foot. No abduction. 6 actuators.
leg_motors: 4x mjbots qdd100 beta 2 (16 Nm peak <1 s, 28.8 rad/s)
wheel_motors: 2x mjbots moteus developer kit (direct drive), 1.7 Nm, 111 rad/s
notes: Mass is summed from the URDF (derived). Cost is 'around $3,000' per the FOSDEM 2026 abstract. Raspberry Pi 4 + mjbots pi3hat. FDM-printed parts in FreeCAD. v2 (2026) uses a stiffer fork lower leg after printed tibias and femurs broke. PPO balancer (ground-velocity action) and mjlab policies.

name: TRON 1 (wheeled-foot configuration)
license: tron1-rl-isaaclab and tron1-mujoco-sim: Apache-2.0; tron1-rl-isaacgym: BSD-3-Clause
leg_topology: unknown from spec page; multi-modal biped with interchangeable point-foot, sole and wheel feet
leg_motors: 48 V joint actuators, 30 Nm rated, 60 Nm peak, 15 rad/s
battery: 46.8 V 4.5 Ah ternary Li, <=2 h, swappable
notes: Height and mass are upper bounds (<=845 mm size, <=20 kg). Wheeled speed <=3 m/s. Intel i3 12th gen. The Isaac Lab repo ships a USD and is the best permissively licensed Isaac Lab wheel-legged starting point.

name: foc-wheel-legged-robot
leg_topology: Closed linkage, 2 body-mounted motors per leg, controlled as a virtual leg (VMC) with LQR gains fitted against leg length
leg_motors: 4x 4010 gimbal BLDC (12 V, 0.22 Nm stall, 125 g, CNY 50)
wheel_motors: 2x 2804 gimbal BLDC direct drive (0.04 Nm stall, CNY 13)
notes: BOM CNY 549 without FPV (~USD 75 at an assumed ~7.2 CNY/USD; conversion not sourced, so price_usd is left null). Mostly 3D printed + acrylic. STM32 CAN FOC drivers, ESP32 + MPU6050, Simscape sim. ~1.8k stars.

name: Micro-Wheeled_leg-Robot
leg_topology: Desktop-scale linkage leg driven by Feetech bus servos
wheel_motors: 2x gimbal BLDC via SimpleFOC (L6234 driver, AS5600 encoders)
notes: No licence file (all rights reserved). ESP32 + MPU6050, web joystick. ~3.8k stars.

name: Venus-1 four-link wheel-legged robot
wheel_motors: 2x DJI M2006 P36 geared + C610 ESC
notes: Cost ~CNY 2,576 without RC. Structure is 3 mm 3240 epoxy (FR4-like) plate; electronics bay printed. Author's defects: geared M2006 backlash causes jitter at the balance point (use direct-drive gimbal wheels); CyberGear must be re-zeroed every power-up; PU wheels came loose; yaw drift.

name: Wheel-legged robot (Multivac11)
leg_topology: Five-bar: joint motor spacing 150 mm, thigh 150 mm, shank 270 mm, virtual leg 95.5-398 mm
leg_motors: 4x Unitree A1 (RS-485, one UART per motor, run at 500 Hz)
notes: No licence file. Body 9.5 kg, each leg linkage 1.626 kg excluding wheel, wheel radius 75 mm.

name: Open Duck Mini v2
maker: Antoine Pirrone (apirrone) and community; sponsored by Hugging Face / Pollen Robotics
license: Apache-2.0 (main repo); Runtime, Playground and reference-motion repos have no licence file
leg_topology: Walking biped (no wheels): 5 DOF per leg (hip yaw, roll, pitch, knee, ankle) + 4 DOF neck/head + 2 hobby-servo antennas
leg_motors: 14x Feetech STS3215 7.4 V '19 kg.cm' bus servos (~EUR 14 each; ~3.35 Nm cap in identified model)
notes: price_usd is the README's 'under $400' bound; the BOM sheet totals EUR 398.10 (EUR 432.34 with expression package) and the Tnkr kit is $600. Mass is summed from MJCF body masses (derived). Fully printed in PLA at 15% infill, TPU soles. Pi Zero 2W, BNO055. Trained in MuJoCo Playground/MJX at 50 Hz with Placo reference motions, imitation reward, BAM actuator models, backlash and 0-3 step delay randomization.

name: Microduck
license: Code Apache-2.0; STL meshes in microduck_rl CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; vendor asks it not be called open-source hardware
leg_topology: Small walking biped (15 servos) with passive roller-skate wheel attachments ('roller mode')
leg_motors: 15 servos (modelled as BAM XL330 models in microduck_rl)
notes: Rockchip RK3566, 50 Hz. Pre-orders opened 2026-08-27. mjlab PPO, 1-2 h to a usable gait at 4096 envs. Models voltage sag and backlash as a passive hinge. Character features: seeded per-robot voice, petting detection, Tamagotchi-style app. Head is 38% of mass.

name: Go2-W (wheeled quadruped, technique reference only)
leg_topology: Quadruped, 3 joints per leg + powered wheel per leg
leg_motors: Unitree joint motors (~45 Nm knee per reseller)
notes: Not a biped; listed because Unitree has no wheel-legged biped. Reseller specs conflict.

name: Beni
notes: Consumer follow-and-film camera robot (Kickstarter, >$2.5 M). 3.86 lb, 17.9 mph top speed, jumps obstacles (10 cm in some reports, 10 in in another), rights itself after falls, climbs stairs by hopping, onboard tracking with no internet, 4K30 camera. Hands-on reviews: tracking still unreliable, not waterproof. Inspiration for Gyropup's character and tricks; Gyropup is ten times heavier and built to be tougher.
